details: relay setup writes no .gitignore: .ci/, .worktrees/, __pycache__ and .pytest_cache show as untracked, so the primary checkout, which the rules say must stay clean, is dirty after bin/wt new and after the first check.
failing_case: Trial: after bin/wt new add-count-unique-words, git status on master showed '?? .worktrees/'; after bin/check it showed .ci/, __pycache__/, .pytest_cache/.
pass_cases: Fresh setup, one check, one bin/wt new: git status --short on the default branch is empty; an existing .gitignore keeps its lines.
findings.summary: A project from relay setup is dirty after its first check

details: CONFIRMED by probe. open(path) in text mode with the default newline translates \r\n to \n on read, and the whole text
is written back. Reachable only for a .gitignore with CRLF endings (a repo started on Windows). Size: 5.
failing_case:
".ci/
foo
.worktrees/
__pycache__/
..." : the two existing lines lost their , so git diff shows them changed,
against the docstring "Existing lines are never changed". Expected: ".ci/\r\nfoo\r\n" kept byte for byte, new lines appended.
fix_hint: Read with newline="" (keeps \r\n) and append the missing lines with open(path, "a", newline=""), adding a newline first
only when the file does not end with one; never rewrite the existing text.
pass_cases:
1. ".ci/
foo
" -> the file starts with the same bytes ".ci/
foo
"; the added lines follow.
findings.summary: an existing CRLF .gitignore is rewritten with LF endings: every existing line shows as changed

details: CONFIRMED by probe: anchored -> added list lacks __pycache__/; neg -> file becomes "!.ci/\n.ci/\n...". The anchor is
harmless for .ci/ and .worktrees/ (they live at the root) but not for caches, which appear in every package folder.
failing_case: a) .gitignore "/__pycache__/\n" in a python project: __pycache__/ is counted as present and not added, so
tests/__pycache__/ (pytest's cache in a subfolder) still shows as untracked. Expected: __pycache__/ added.
b) .gitignore "!.ci/\n" (the owner un-ignored .ci on purpose): setup appends ".ci/" after it, which re-ignores .ci.
Expected: the owner's negation left in force (.ci/ not added, or said in the done list).
fix_hint: Treat a leading "/" as present only for the root folders (.ci/, the worktrees folder), not for the stack caches; skip a
line whose name the file names with a leading "!". Or ask git: `git check-ignore -q <probe path>` per line, with a
pass_cases: 2. "!.ci/\n" -> ".ci/" is not added; `git check-ignore .ci/x` stays not-ignored.
3. ".ci\n/.worktrees\n" -> neither .ci/ nor .worktrees/ is added (today's behaviour; /.worktrees is root-anchored, which is where the folder lives).
reason: tests/test_setup.py:93,97,102 pass; the first two fail at 49674b0.
findings.summary: the presence test compares text with slashes stripped, not what git ignores: an anchored entry counts as present, a negated one is overridden

details: CONFIRMED by probe. folder.strip("/") turns an absolute path into a relative-looking pattern. Nothing in relay limits
the key to an inside folder (only this code reads it). Size: 5.
failing_case: Neither pattern matches anything git sees; the owner's file gets a junk line. Expected: no worktrees line for a folder
outside the project (and .ci/ plus the caches still added).
fix_hint: In gitignore_lines, drop the worktrees line when os.path.isabs(folder) or the normalised path starts with "..".
pass_cases: 1. worktrees = "/Users/x/wt" -> added lines are .ci/ and the stack caches only.
findings.summary: a worktrees folder outside the project (absolute or ../) becomes a meaningless .gitignore line

details: CONFIRMED by reading: both new tests use a fresh project, where kit.toml is written with worktrees = ".worktrees",
equal to the fallback. The code path is correct today (probe with worktrees="/Users/x/wt" shows the value is read).
evidence: grep -n 'worktrees' tests/test_setup.py tests/test_setup_off.py: only ".worktrees/t/f" and "/.worktrees" inputs.

pass, though the item promises "the worktrees folder from kit.toml". Expected: a test that fails on that change.
fix_hint: Add a test: write .claude/kit.toml with [project] worktrees = "trees" before setup, assert "trees/" in the .gitignore lines.
pass_cases: 1. Project with .claude/kit.toml [project] worktrees = "trees", setup run -> .gitignore has "trees/" and not ".worktrees/".
reason: tests/test_setup.py:111 and :116 read worktrees "trees" from kit.toml and assert trees/ and not .worktrees/, so a hardcoded folder fails them (read; not run against a hardcoded variant). They pass at 49674b0 by design, as the code already read the key.

details: CONFIRMED by grep: no "gitignore" in docs/setup.md. The doc is the contract of what setup touches in a person's
evidence: git grep -n -i gitignore -- docs plugins/relay/README.md README.md -> no line in docs/setup.md
